output.title: Check the process before you automate it
output.body:
Before you build a regression suite around a workflow, decide whether the workflow itself is stable enough to deserve one. For an owner-operator, that means picking one repeatable task — customer questions, invoices, or data work — and asking a simple question: does it produce the same kind of output most times, or do people handle exceptions differently each week?

If the manual process is already inconsistent, automation will only repeat the inconsistency faster. The better check is more basic: can you describe the task clearly enough that someone else would follow the same steps and get the same result?

That is why the first step is to document one workflow on a single page: trigger, inputs, steps, edge cases, and the point where a human still needs to check the work. If you can’t write that down cleanly, the workflow is not ready for automation yet.

Bareni’s diagnostic starts there: identify one recurring workflow, be honest about whether AI fits, and only then decide whether to keep it manual, standardise it first, or automate part of it later. The paper version usually tells you where the process breaks before software does.
